diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that \Cref{assumption:operator}(i) and \Cref{assumption:operator}(ii) holds and that $\{X(t)\}_t$ satisfies \Cref{eq:stochastic-convolution}.
Define $\omega_k(t) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda_k}} \inprod{W_Q(t)}{e_k}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The variance of the defined coordinate is t⟨Qe_k,e_k⟩/λ_k, not necessarily t. Assumptions (i) and (ii) do not identify the A-eigenvector e_k with the Q-eigenvector belonging to λ_k. Merely permuting two Q-eigenvectors with unequal eigenvalues gives a counterexample. The covariance identification needed for standardness is available only under the additional joint-basis hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore the processes $\{\omega_k(t)\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ are $\mathbb{R}$-valued, standard Wiener-processes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For positive-variance coordinates, normalize by v_k=⟨Qe_k,e_k⟩ and use √v_k in the coefficient formula. Under assumption (iii), v_k=λ_k and the later formulas are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's assertion for non-joint eigenbases is false. Later results already assuming the joint basis are not invalidated by this particular defect.
issues.title: The Wiener coordinates are not standardized without a joint eigenbasis
issues.why_classification: A local covariance normalization corrects the lemma without changing the numerical schemes, convergence rates, or subsequent joint-basis results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $Q$ has an orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions $\{f_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$, spanning $\mathcal{L}^2(\mathcal{D})$, with corresponding eigenvalues $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$

issues.failure_explanation: Neither the lemma nor the operator assumptions require positive covariance eigenvalues. For example, Q=0 and W_Q=0 satisfy the stated covariance and spectral requirements, but every displayed coordinate is 0/0. Thus the asserted family of standard Wiener processes is not defined even in the joint-basis setting.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize only positive-variance modes. In the joint basis, set c_k=0 when λ_k=0 and omit those modes from stochastic-integral calculations, or introduce unused auxiliary Brownian motions for them.
issues.overall_effect: The coefficient representation and its use in the spectral proof do not cover the permitted zero-noise modes as written.
issues.title: Zero covariance eigenvalues make the coordinate definition undefined
issues.why_classification: Separating zero modes is a routine degenerate-case repair that preserves all error bounds and admissible covariance operators.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Delta := \sum_{k = 1}^d \frac{\partial^2}{\partial x_k^2}$ be defined on a subset $D(\Delta)$ of $\LD$ of sufficiently smooth functions which are zero on $\partial \mathcal{D}$, the boundary of $\mathcal{D}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Being defined on a subset of smooth zero-boundary functions does not specify the self-adjoint Dirichlet realization. On (0,1), the choice D(Δ)=C_c^∞(0,1) satisfies the stated domain description but has no nonzero eigenfunctions: a compactly supported solution of −u''=ξu must vanish identically. The claimed eigenbasis therefore does not follow from the stated hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Then the operator $A := -\Delta$ has a set of orthonormal eigenfunctions $\{e_k\}_k$ spanning $\LD$, with a corresponding non-decreasing sequence of positive eigenvalues $\{\xi_k\}_k$ satisfying the estimates

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the standard self-adjoint Dirichlet Laplacian, for example with weak domain {u∈H_0^1(𝒟): Δu∈L²(𝒟)}, rather than an arbitrary smooth subdomain.
issues.overall_effect: The supporting spectral lemma, and hence its application to fractional powers of the Laplacian, needs a specified operator realization.
issues.title: The Laplacian domain hypothesis does not ensure an eigenbasis
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard operator realization is a local hypothesis repair preserving the domains, spectral rates, and intended PDE model.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus $A$ and $Q$ have eigenvalues $\mu_k = r^{-1}(\kappa^2 + \xi_k)^{\alpha}$ and $\lambda_k = \sigma r^{-\gamma}(\kappa^2 + \xi_k)^{-\beta}$
satisfy the bounds $r^{-1} C_\Delta k^{\frac{2 \alpha}{d}}\leq \mu_k$ and $\lambda_k \leq \sigma r^{-\gamma} C_\Delta k^{- \frac{2 \beta}{d}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Laplacian lower bound gives C_1=r^{-1}C_Δ^α and C_2=σr^{-γ}C_Δ^{-β}, not the constants used in the proof. Consequently the spectral constant must contain C_Δ^{-β−α(2γ−1)}. The printed constant can fail: with γ=α=β=1 on a long interval and κ equal to the inverse interval length, its M=1 bound is independent of interval length while even one omitted mode's variance grows without bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use C_1=r^{-1}C_Δ^α and C_2=σr^{-γ}C_Δ^{-β}, replacing C_Δ^{2−2γ} in the corollary by C_Δ^{-β−α(2γ−1)}.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit error constant is unreliable, although the stated spectral power of M is supported.
issues.title: The Laplacian spectral error constant uses incorrect powers
issues.why_classification: Correcting the eigenvalue scaling and constant is local and preserves the convergence rate and parameter regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that $\Pi_m$ is such that $\Pi_m g = g$ for all $g \in \mathcal{P}_m(\mathcal{I})$ and that $\Pi_m$ satisfies $\norm{\Pi_m h}_{\mathcal{L}^2([0,t))} \leq C_\Pi \norm{h}_{\mathcal{L}^2([0,t))}$ for some $C_\Pi > 0$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses additivity of Π_m, but only a bounded map fixing the polynomial space is assumed. Define Π_m u=u for u in that space and Π_m u=0 otherwise. This satisfies the stated norm bound with C_Π=1, even in every L^p norm. For m=0 and γ=2, however, Π_m f_t=0 on every mesh, so the stochastic approximation does not converge at all.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require Π_m to be linear on the span of the piecewise-polynomial space and f_t, or impose an equivalent difference bound that justifies the displayed quasi-optimality step.
issues.overall_effect: The general temporal and full-discretisation guarantees are false for the stated class of maps. The particular linear projection and sampling schemes do not exhibit this counterexample.
issues.title: Bounded polynomial reproduction does not imply quasi-optimality
issues.why_classification: The missing standard projection hypothesis is local, is satisfied by the intended schemes, and makes the existing approximation argument applicable without changing rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \left(\EV{\abs{c_k(t) - \Tilde{c}^{(m)}_k(t)}^2} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}} & \leq \frac{\sqrt{\lambda_k}}{\Gamma(\gamma)} \norm{f_t - \Pi_m f_t}_{\mathcal{L}^2([0,t))}
& \leq \frac{\sqrt{\lambda_k}}{\Gamma(\gamma)} (1 + C_\Pi) \abs{K_{m + 1}} \max \left(\frac{C_{op}(\gamma)}{m!}, C\right) \left(1 +\sqrt{\log(t h^{-1})} \right) h^{m + 1}

issues.failure_explanation: Squaring the proved root-mean-square estimates produces λ_k δ_{γ,h}², and λ_k μ_k^{-2/q} in the refined estimate, rather than the printed root factors. The λ_k dependence is false by scaling the noise. The critical logarithm is also genuinely too small: for m=0, γ=3/2, and uniform-cell L² projection, the squared approximation error is of order h² log(1/h), not h²√log(1/h).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Square all factors in the root-mean-square estimates consistently. State mean-square bounds with λ_k δ_{γ,h}² and the refined factor λ_k μ_k^{-2/q}, and propagate the squared logarithmic factor to the corollaries and main theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The scalar mean-square constants are incorrect, and the temporal and full-discretisation bounds overstate the rate at γ=m+3/2.
issues.title: Root-mean-square bounds are misstated as mean-square bounds
issues.why_classification: The existing proof supports the correction, but it requires a substantive weakening of the claimed critical logarithmic rate and changes the stated noise-scaling guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $t \in [0,T]$, $\mu_k > 0$, $\lambda_k > 0$, $\gamma > \frac{1}{2}$, and define $h := \max_{\ell}(t_\ell - t_{\ell - 1})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses do not imply h≤t. For example, t=T/4 and a two-cell uniform partition give t/h=1/2, so the square root has a negative argument. At t=0 the logarithm is undefined. Even the grid-point corollary permits t_n<h on a nonuniform mesh because h is the maximum over the full partition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a globally defined factor such as 1+√log(1+t/h), take ε=min(h,t) in the regularisation argument, and handle t=0 directly.
issues.overall_effect: The critical-case estimates are not real-valued statements for part of their stated time and mesh range.
issues.title: The critical logarithmic factor is undefined for allowed times
issues.why_classification: This is a local boundary-case repair that retains the time range and the asymptotic logarithmic order.

issues.failure_explanation: There is no requirement b≤t. For an allowed fractional value such as γ=3/4, t=1, and [a,b)=[2,3), the displayed power is not a real-valued function, so its asserted real L² projection and the coefficient formulas are not defined.

failure_location.quote: Define $s \mapsto (t - s)^{\gamma - 1}$ as a function on $[a,b) \subset [0, \infty)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require 0≤a<b≤t, with the standing γ>1/2 assumption, before defining the projection and its integrals.
issues.overall_effect: The computational lemma does not hold on all intervals admitted by its statement.
issues.title: The projection-computation lemma permits intervals beyond the kernel domain
issues.why_classification: The missing local domain condition preserves every interval needed for the intended stochastic convolution.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: define $\Pi_0: C([0,t_n)) \rightarrow \mathcal{P}_0(\mathcal{I})$ by $\Pi_0: f \mapsto \sum_{\ell = 1}^{n} f(t_{\ell - 1} + \theta (t_\ell - t_{\ell - 1})) \mathbb{I}_{[t_{\ell - 1}, t_\ell)}(s)$
Then $g$ is of the form $g(s) = \sum_{\ell = 1}^{N} g_\ell \mathbb{I}_{[t_{\ell - 1}, t_\ell)}(s)$

issues.failure_explanation: At θ=1 the formula evaluates at t_n, outside its declared domain. At interior nodes, the half-open representative of g takes the next cell's value, so Π_0 does not reproduce piecewise constants. If t_n<T and the full-mesh representative is used, take α=0 and g zero before t_n but one on the following cell. Its input norm on [0,t_n) is zero, while the last sampled cell is nonzero, contradicting the asserted bound.

failure_location.quote: Then, assuming $\theta \in [0,1)$, or assuming $\gamma > 1$ and $\theta \in [0,1]$, there exists $C_\Pi > 0$ such that $\norm{\Pi_0 h}_{\mathcal{L}^2([0,t_n))} \leq C_\Pi \norm{h}_{\mathcal{L}^2([0,t_n))}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For θ=1, define sampling by the left-hand trace from each cell, including at t_n. This reproduces g on its own cell and agrees with endpoint evaluation of f_{t_n} when γ>1.
issues.overall_effect: The endpoint extension θ=1 is not justified by the stated operator and stability lemma.
issues.title: Right-endpoint sampling is not defined consistently on piecewise-constant inputs
issues.why_classification: A standard one-sided endpoint convention fixes the operator without changing the intended quadrature values or convergence regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for all $h: [0,t_n) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ of the form $h(s) = g(s) + \alpha f_{t_n}(s)$ where $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ and $g \in \mathcal{P}_0(\mathcal{I})$

issues.failure_explanation: The factor αg_ℓ can have either sign, so positive-factor comparison estimates cannot be multiplied by it without reversing inequalities. Moreover, comparing endpoint powers separately does not justify comparing their differences. The final quadratic-form bound does not follow by combining separate coefficient bounds: cancellation can make g_ℓ+αf very small. A uniform estimate controlling this cancellation is missing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Center f on each cell by its mean and prove h_ℓ|f(ŝ_ℓ)−mean(f)|²≤C∫|f−mean(f)|². Complete the square in g_ℓ+αmean(f). The distance-comparison lemma controls nonterminal cells, and the terminal-cell power integrals can be evaluated explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The mesh-uniform stability needed for the point-sampling convergence corollary is not proved, including for θ<1.
issues.title: The sampling-stability proof does not control signed cross terms
issues.why_classification: The core stability argument needs a contained but nontrivial replacement quadratic-form estimate; the existing termwise comparison cannot be repaired by changing a sign.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exists an $r_{\mu} > 0$ and a $C_1 > 0$ such that $\{\mu_k\}_{k = 1}^\infty$ satisfies
then $C^{''}_M = \frac{C}{\Gamma(\gamma)^2} \sum_{k = 1}^M \mu_k^{-\frac{2}{q}} \lambda_k$.

issues.failure_explanation: A bounded inverse requires only sup_k μ_k^{-1}<∞, not summability. Finite partial sums are also not evidence of convergence as M grows. For example, μ_k=k^{1/2} and λ_k=k^{-1/4} give bounded A^{-1} and bounded Q, but ∑μ_k^{-1}λ_k=∑k^{-3/4} diverges. These power bounds satisfy the solution summability condition at γ=5/2, so temporal smoothness does not repair the inference.

failure_location.quote: In most practical applications $A$ will have bounded inverse, i.e., $\sum_{k = 1}^M \mu_k^{-1} < \infty$, so that in the extreme case of $\gamma > m + \frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{2}$ we have convergence of $\sum_{k = 1}^M \mu_k^{-1} \lambda_k$ assuming only that $Q$ is bounded.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require a trace-class inverse, or directly require ∑μ_k^{-1}λ_k<∞. For a guarantee covering every bounded Q, a sufficient source-supported growth condition is r_μ>1.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed M-uniform temporal constant under merely bounded Q is unsupported in the stated spectral regime. The main theorem's finite-M estimates do not themselves assert this false implication.
issues.title: Bounded inverse is confused with trace-class inverse
issues.why_classification: The summability guarantee needs a genuine additional spectral restriction, although the finite-dimensional estimates and two-parameter convergence remain available.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: More specifically we let $\mathcal{I} := \{t_\ell\}_{\ell = 0}^N$ be a discretisation of $[0,T]$ such that $0 = t_0 < t_1 < ... < t_N = T$.
where $h_\ell := t_\ell - t_{\ell - 1}$.

The asserted common variance, and hence the suggested i.i.d. sampling law, is correct only for a uniform mesh.

failure_location.quote: are then i.i.d. Gaussian variables, with mean $0$ and variance $\int_0^h \e^{-2\mu_k u} \text{d} u = \frac{1}{2 \mu_k} (1 - \e^{-2 \mu_k h})$, and are therefore easily simulated.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the variables as independent and sample each with its own variance (1−exp(−2μ_k h_ℓ))/(2μ_k).
issues.overall_effect: Using the stated common-variance sampling description on a nonuniform grid generates the wrong driving-noise law.
issues.title: Nonuniform-step noise integrals are incorrectly declared identically distributed
issues.why_classification: A local variance correction preserves the algorithm, nonuniform-mesh scope, and all convergence rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \Tilde{c}_k^{(m)}(t) := \frac{\sqrt{\lambda_k}}{\Gamma(\gamma)} \int_0^t \e^{-\mu_k (t-s)} \left( \Pi_m f_t \right) \text{d} \omega_k(s)
More specifically we let $\mathcal{I} := \{t_\ell\}_{\ell = 0}^N$ be a discretisation of $[0,T]$ such that $0 = t_0 < t_1 < ... < t_N = T$.

issues.failure_explanation: The expanded simulation sums all N cell integrals through T even when the requested evaluation time is t<T. In particular, at t=t_n it includes independent increments from cells ℓ>n, which are absent from the defining integral over [0,t]. Their variance does not disappear under mesh refinement, so this is not an implementation of the stated approximation at intermediate times.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the partition restricted to [0,t]: sum only completed cells before t, include a final partial cell when necessary, and compute the corresponding projection coefficients on those cells.
issues.overall_effect: The printed higher-order executable expansion is incorrect away from the final time and is not covered by the convergence guarantees for the integral-defined method.
issues.title: The higher-order simulation formula includes future noise
issues.why_classification: Routine truncation and partial-cell handling restore the intended algorithm for every evaluation time without new analysis or rate loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\alpha > 0$, $\beta > 0$, $\sigma > 0$, $r > 0$, and $\kappa > 0$.
\nu_t = \gamma - \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2\alpha}\min \left(\beta - \frac{d}{2}, 0 \right)

At β_s=1 it gives β=0, so Q has constant eigenvalues and cannot satisfy the required negative decay exponent. These failures remain after correcting the separate factor-of-two error in α.

failure_location.quote: This reparametrisation specifies $A$ and $Q$ through the spatial smoothness $\nu_s > 0$, the temporal smoothness $\nu_t > 0$, the spatial range $r_s > 0$, the temporal range $r_t > 0$, and a ``non-separability'' parameter $0 \leq \beta_s \leq 1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat the endpoints explicitly: allow α=0 or β=0, allow zero spectral exponents where the same summability inequality holds, and define ν_t=γ−1/2 when α=0. The existing spectral tail calculation then applies to the endpoint cases.
issues.overall_effect: The stated closed input range includes two degenerate models not covered by the operator assumptions or by the parameter formulas as written.
issues.title: The advertised non-separability endpoints are outside the proved hypotheses
issues.why_classification: Standard degenerate-case definitions and non-strict spectral exponents preserve the advertised parameter range and the existing rates without new proof architecture.
